questions.question: What is the main reason to wrap examples in `<example>` tags inside an `<examples>` block?
options: It is required for the model to read them at all
It reduces the token count of the examples
It clearly separates demonstrations from the real input so they are not confused
It makes the model ignore the examples' format
questions.explanation: Tags delimit each example and keep demonstrations distinct from the actual input to be processed.

questions.question: All of your example replies start with "Dear Sir/Madam". What problem is likely?
options: The model copies that greeting into every reply, even where it does not fit
The model refuses to use any greeting
The model ignores the examples entirely
Nothing, since models only copy the task, not the wording
questions.explanation: Models over-fit to shared surface features; vary incidental features or state explicitly which aspects to copy.

questions.question: Which set of examples is best for a ticket classifier?
options: Five short, polite examples from the most common category
Examples covering every category, varied in length and tone, including boundary cases
One very long example that mentions all categories
Invented examples that are all perfectly formatted
questions.explanation: Diverse, representative examples that include rare categories and hard cases teach the real rule rather than incidental patterns.

questions.question: If an example contradicts your written instructions, what often happens?
options: The model always follows the instructions
The model averages the two behaviours exactly
The model often follows the example, so instructions and examples must be consistent
questions.explanation: Examples are copied very faithfully and can override instructions, so check that they agree.
